correctness.rationale: Since the disjoint finite block supports escape, b_n(x)→0 on c0 and the codomain limit exists. The nth ℓ1 row norm is strictly <κ+(1-κ)t_n<1, but these norms tend to 1 because mass u on block supports vanishes; the limit row norm is κ<1. Any norming z∈ℓ∞ for T** must have |〈u,z〉|=1, forcing a common sign on supp u and hence σ〈b_n,z〉≤1−2D_n. Conversely a single z equal to this sign on supp u and matching b_n off it achieves equality simultaneously on disjoint blocks, giving norm 1 exactly when liminf D_n=0. The ℓ1 simplex is complete; finite-support cores are dense and eventually D_n=0; full-support cores form dense Gδ and D_n=1/2, so the attaining locus is dense meagre. Canonical pair criterion and the triple-block example with D_n=1/(4n) check signs and scope. This is an analytic infinite-dimensional proof, no finite simulation can replace it.
